keyFindings.description: Every failed settle (a first send, the stranded resend, a person's Retry at any age) reopens comment.created whenever the comment mentions the session and its own topic is not in published_destinations. The re-scan publishes to every destination not yet recorded, read from the issue as it is now: a moved route, a new claimant, new followers or document authors get the old comment. published_at moves (and is null between), which deliveryaudit reads as when the comment was published. Reproduced with a throwaway outbox test. Reopen only where the outbox left the copy to this attempt (a resumed attempt it published past), and publish only the owed session's copy.

A rolling update from a build before this one runs the old outbox beside the new API: the old outbox publishes a copy for an attempt pending over a minute without settling it (the new sender then sends the mention too), and marks a reopened event published with no claim token. Name it and bound it in the body's risk lines (who is affected, and Recreate as the alternative), or make the new API safe against it.
